docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: Managed Care Plans (MCPs) must administer both Enhanced Care Management (ECM) and Community Supports.
explanation: The policy states, "CalOptima Health and its Health Networks shall coordinate care for Members enrolled in Enhanced Care Management (ECM) and/or Community Supports," and also that they "shall ensure compliance with all applicable State and federal requirements related to ECM requirements," directly indicating the plan administers both programs.

explanation: The policy states that CalOptima Health shall identify members for Community Supports by 'Working with ECM Providers to identify Members receiving ECM' and 'Accepting CalOptima Health Community Supports requests from Providers and other community-based entities,' directly demonstrating collaboration with community-based providers in administering these services.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide

obligation: When a Member under 21 is served in Enhanced Care Management (ECM) and does not meet the adult ECM criteria upon turning 21, the ECM Provider and Managed Care Plan (MCP) should apply the MCP’s usual, DHCS-approved “graduation” criteria to determine when the Member is ready to disenroll.
explanation: The P&P explicitly states that ECM Providers should reassess members against their ECM discontinuation criteria, not the ECM Population of Focus eligibility criteria, to evaluate whether members are ready to transition out of ECM. docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: For children and youth, MCPs should establish robust referral pathways with all pediatric providers.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide

explanation: The P&P references APL 22-005, which the obligation explicitly states describes the member identification process. docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: When MCPs are not able to contract with the county behavioral health agency or its subcontracted provider as the ECM Provider, the ECM Provider for a Member within this population should have experience and expertise working with individuals with serious mental health needs and SUD, as well as the ability to adequately coordinate services across multiple delivery systems.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs should partner with local programs serving pregnant and postpartum individuals to help with identification, including Comprehensive Perinatal Services Program (CPSP), Black Infant Health (BIH) Program, California Perinatal Equity Initiative (PEI), county First 5s, Indian Health Program, American Indian Maternal Support Services (AIMSS), CDPH’s California Home Visiting Program (CHVP), CDSS’ CalWORKs Home Visiting Program (HVP), county behavioral health programs, local Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) agencies, local food banks, local diaper banks, and CBOs supporting individuals experiencing intimate partner violence.

obligation: MCPs will assign every Member authorized for ECM to an ECM Provider.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The care plan must leverage Member strengths and preferences and make recommendations for service needs.

explanation: The P&P explicitly states, "Enhanced coordination of care... in order to ensure that the Member’s care is continuous and integrated among all service providers," and further, "The ECM Provider will work to ensure care is continuous and integrated among all service providers," directly addressing the obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: Enhanced Coordination of Care services must include referring to and following up with primary care, physical and developmental health, mental health, SUD treatment, LTSS, oral health, palliative care, and necessary community-based and social services, including housing, as needed.
explanation: The candidate explicitly states that 'The ECM Provider will... refer to and follow up with primary care, physical and developmental health, mental health, SUD treatment, LTSS, oral health, Palliative Care, and necessary community-based and social services, including housing, as needed,' directly matching the obligation's requirements for Enhanced Coordination of Care services.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: Enhanced Coordination of Care services must include providing support to engage the Member in their treatment, including coordination for medication review and/or reconciliation.
explanation: The P&P explicitly states under 'Enhanced Coordination of Care' that 'The ECM Provider will engage the ECM Member in their treatment, including coordination for medication review and/or medication reconciliation,' directly matching the obligation's requirements.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The Member’s needs and preferences must be communicated in a timely manner to the Member’s multi-disciplinary care team to ensure safe, appropriate, and effective person-centered care.
explanation: The candidate explicitly states, "The ECM Provider will communicate the ECM Member’s needs and preferences timely to the Member’s multi-disciplinary care team in a manner that ensures safe, appropriate, and effective person-centered care," which directly matches all components of the obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: Regular contact must be ensured with the Member (and/or their parent, caregiver, guardian) when appropriate, consistent with the care plan, and to ensure information is shared with all involved parties to monitor the Member’s conditions, health status, care planning, medication usages, and side effects.
explanation: The candidate explicitly states that the ECM Provider will "ensure regular contact with the ECM Member and their family members, legal guardians, Authorized Representatives, caregivers, and authorized support persons, as appropriate, consistent with the CMP and to ensure information is shared with all involved parties to monitor the ECM Member’s conditions, health status, care planning, medications usages and side effects," directly matching all requirements of the obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The assigned ECM Lead Care Manager is responsible for ensuring that BPHM is in place as part of the Members’ care management, as established in the PHM Policy Guide.
explanation: The candidate states that an 'ECM Provider shall ensure Basic Population Health Management (BPHM) is provided', but the obligation specifically assigns this responsibility to the 'assigned ECM Lead Care Manager'. While the Lead Care Manager works for the ECM Provider, the policy does not explicitly state the LCM's responsibility for ensuring BPHM.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: ECM Providers should provide information to the hospital discharge planners or discharging facility staff about ECM.
explanation: The policy requires ECM Providers to have processes to "engage and cooperate with area hospitals" and "share ECM Member care plans with other Providers involved in each ECM Member’s care." While this implies information exchange with hospital staff, it does not explicitly state that ECM Providers must provide general information about ECM to hospital discharge planners or discharging facility staff.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs must ensure that ECM Providers have access to or are provided ADT feed data information for enrolled Members to provide transitional care services for ECM Members.
explanation: The policy states that "CalOptima Health shall ensure the TCS Assigned Care Managers, ECM LCM, or CCM Care Manager are notified... through an ADT Feed notification." This directly addresses the requirement for ECM Providers (or their associated care managers) to be provided ADT feed data for transitional care services, as 'TCS Assigned Care Managers' explicitly links the notification to the purpose of transitional care.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: For Members who are experiencing or are likely to experience a care transition, the ECM Lead Care Manager must develop and regularly update a discharge planning document for the Member.
explanation: The candidate states the ECM LCM is responsible for ensuring collaboration and coordination to facilitate safe transitions, including discharge planning documentation that incorporates instructions developed by facility staff. This implies involvement with the document but does not explicitly state the ECM LCM must develop and regularly update the entire discharge planning document.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The plan must ensure the completion of discharge risk assessment.
explanation: The P&P explicitly states, "A discharge risk assessment will be completed prior to discharge," directly addressing the obligation for the plan to ensure the completion of discharge risk assessment.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The plan must coordinate any follow up provider appointments and support services to facilitate safe and appropriate transitions from one setting or level of care to another.
explanation: The policy explicitly states that the Care Manager "shall ensure needed post-discharge services are provided and Referrals are made, follow-ups are scheduled and completed, including, but not limited to: Assisting with making follow up Provider appointments" and lists various support services and referrals, all within the context of transitions for high-risk members.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The plan must coordinate medication review/reconciliation.
explanation: The P&P explicitly states that the ECM Provider will engage the ECM Member in their treatment, 'including coordination for medication review and/or medication reconciliation,' directly matching the obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The plan must provide adherence support.
explanation: The policy explicitly states that documentation for participant noncompliance with any aspect of the Plan of Care "shall include employee efforts to obtain compliance," which directly demonstrates the plan's provision of adherence support.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The plan must provide referral to appropriate services.
explanation: The policy explicitly states, "Refer Members to culturally and linguistically appropriate community services, as needed," directly addressing the obligation to provide referrals to appropriate services.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The plan must document a Member’s authorized parent, caregiver, guardian, other family member(s) and/or other authorized support person(s).
explanation: The policy explicitly states that if an Authorization is signed by a Member’s Personal Representative, a description of their authority to act for the Member must be provided, listing examples like parent and court-appointed guardian, which directly aligns with documenting authorized support persons.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The plan must ensure all required authorizations are in place to ensure effective communication between the ECM Providers; the Member and/or their Member’s authorized parent, caregiver, guardian, other family member(s) and/or other authorized support person(s), as applicable.
explanation: The candidate explicitly states the need to 'Keep records of... authorizations necessary for sharing personally identifiable information' between ECM Providers, other Providers, and family members/support persons. This directly addresses the obligation for all required authorizations to be in place for effective communication among these parties.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The plan must conduct activities to ensure the Member and/or parent, caregiver, guardian, other family member(s) and/or other authorized support person(s) are knowledgeable about the Member’s condition(s), with the overall goal of improving the Member’s care planning and follow-up, adherence to treatment, and medication management, in accordance with federal, state, and local privacy and confidentiality laws.
explanation: The candidate explicitly states that the ECM Provider shall conduct activities, including educating the specified individuals to ensure they are knowledgeable about the Member’s conditions, with the goal of improving care planning, follow-up, adherence to treatment, and medication management, all in accordance with privacy laws. This directly matches all aspects of the obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The plan must ensure the Member’s ECM Lead Care Manager serves as the primary point of contact for the Member and/or parent, caregiver, guardian, other family member(s) and/or other authorized support person(s).
explanation: The P&P explicitly states, "The ECM Provider shall ensure that the ECM Member’s assigned ECM LCM serves as the primary point of contact for the ECM Member and their family members, legal guardians, Authorized Representatives, caregivers, and other authorized support persons, as applicable," directly matching the obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The plan must identify supports needed for the Member and/or their parent, caregiver, guardian, other family member(s) and/or other authorized support person(s) to manage the Member’s condition.
explanation: The P&P explicitly states an "Evaluation for adequacy of caregiver resources, such as family or other support person involvement" and requires documentation of "specific gaps to address" to ensure resources are "sufficient for the Member’s needs," directly aligning with the obligation to identify supports for various individuals to manage the Member's condition.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The plan must assist the Member and/or their parent, caregiver, guardian, other family member(s) and/or other authorized support person(s) in accessing needed support services.
explanation: The candidate states the plan shall "assist the Member, Member’s Authorized Representative... with any additional or immediate needs," which covers the Member and authorized support persons in accessing needs. However, it does not explicitly list parents, caregivers, guardians, or other family members as recipients of this assistance unless they are also an Authorized Representative, leading to partial coverage of the specified parties.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The plan must assist the Member and/or their parent, caregiver, guardian, other family member(s) and/or other authorized support person(s) with making informed choices.
explanation: The policy explicitly states that CalOptima Health shall provide Person-Centered Planning, which includes 'Facilitating and encouraging the full participation of the Member... and with the Member’s consent, the Member’s family, caregiver or friends... in Discussions and decisions regarding the Member’s treatments and services' and 'Ensuring that the Member receives all necessary information regarding treatment and services required to make an informed choice.' This directly addresses the plan assisting the specified parties with making informed choices.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The plan must provide appropriate education to the Member's parent, caregiver, guardian, other family member(s), and/or other authorized support person(s) about care instructions for the Member.
explanation: The policy explicitly states that the ECM Provider will ensure regular contact with 'family members, legal guardians, Authorized Representatives, caregivers, and authorized support persons' to 'ensure information is shared' regarding 'care planning, medications usages and side effects,' which directly addresses providing education about care instructions to the specified individuals.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The plan must ensure that the Member's parent, caregiver, guardian, other family member(s), and/or other authorized support person(s) has a copy of their care plan and information about how to request updates.
explanation: The P&P states the plan "shall update the ICP... and disseminate the ICP to the member... caregiver or Authorized Representative," which directly addresses providing a copy of the care plan to some specified support persons. However, it does not explicitly state that these support persons are provided with information on how to request updates to the care plan.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The ECM Lead Care Manager must know every component of the Member’s needs and services and ensure that they are coordinated.
explanation: The P&P states that the ECM Lead Care Manager (LCM) is responsible for engaging with a multi-disciplinary care team to 'Identify gaps in the ECM Member’s care' and 'Ensure appropriate input is obtained to effectively coordinate all primary, medical, behavioral, developmental, and oral health needs, Long Term Services and Supports (LTSS), Community Supports offered by CalOptima Health, and other services that address Social Drivers of Health regardless of setting, at a minimum'. This explicitly covers knowing every component of the Member's needs and ensuring their coordination.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs are responsible for ensuring that services provided through ECM do not duplicate services from any other program(s).
explanation: The candidate explicitly states that 'CalOptima Health shall ensure non-duplication of services provided through ECM and any other covered benefit, program, and/or delivery system,' directly matching the obligation for MCPs to ensure ECM services do not duplicate other programs.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs should regularly check available data feeds to evaluate which of their Members might be enrolled in other programs that provide care coordination.
explanation: The P&P explicitly states that 'Data feed from DHCS when available is evaluated routinely to identify Members open in TCM and Case Management,' directly addressing the obligation to regularly check data feeds to identify members in other care coordination programs.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs should establish processes and requirements to ensure ECM Providers ask Members about their participation in other programs as part of the in-person comprehensive assessment and care planning process.
explanation: The P&P requires ECM Providers to conduct a comprehensive assessment primarily through in-person contact to assess member needs and ensure care is integrated among all service providers across all delivery systems. While this strongly implies asking about participation in other programs, the policy does not explicitly state this requirement.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: If ECM is being provided in addition to an existing care management program, the existing program must not be discontinued.
explanation: No candidate explicitly states that an existing care management program must not be discontinued if Enhanced Care Management (ECM) is provided in addition to it. The candidates discuss discontinuing ECM, transitioning out of ECM, or avoiding duplication between other specific services, but not the specific scenario outlined in the obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: Adult, child, and youth MCP Members cannot be enrolled in both ECM and a 1915(c) waiver program at the same time.
explanation: The P&P explicitly states, "A Member shall not be eligible for ECM while enrolled in the following programs: a. 1915(c) waivers," directly addressing the obligation that members cannot be enrolled in both ECM and a 1915(c) waiver program simultaneously.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The MCP should ensure that if a Member is receiving ECM and a slot to enroll in a 1915(c) waiver program becomes available, the Member has the choice of whether to continue receiving ECM or enroll in the 1915(c) waiver program.
explanation: The obligation states a member has a choice to continue ECM or enroll in a 1915(c) waiver. However, the P&P explicitly states, 'A Member shall not be eligible for ECM while enrolled in the following programs: a. 1915(c) waivers,' which directly contradicts the member's ability to choose to continue ECM if they enroll in a 1915(c) waiver program.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The MCP should provide education to the Member about their options, including describing what is available through the ECM benefit compared with 1915(c) waiver programs, so the Member can make an informed decision.
explanation: No candidate explicitly states that the MCP provides education to members describing what is available through the ECM benefit compared with 1915(c) waiver programs to enable an informed decision. While some candidates mention general member education or informed choices, or refer to 1915(c) waivers as an eligibility exclusion, none directly address the specific comparative education requirement.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The MCP must ensure non-duplication of services between ECM and CCS.
explanation: The candidate explicitly states that CalOptima Health shall ensure non-duplication of services provided through ECM and any other covered benefit, program, and/or delivery system, which directly covers the obligation regarding CCS.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The MCP must ensure that family (and child when mature enough) participation and collaboration in the plan of care are solicited as part of Patient and Family Teaching services.
explanation: The policy addresses providing families with "information, education, and support" (Patient and Family Teaching services) so they "understand the goals, treatment plan, and course of care for their child or youth and their role in the process" (participation and collaboration in the plan of care). However, it implies rather than explicitly states that participation is "solicited."

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The MCP must ensure that education is provided to parents and family members about the system of care and services (including social services) available as part of Patient and Family Teaching services.
explanation: The P&P excerpt explicitly states that 'families know where to go for ongoing information, education, and support in order that they understand... what it means to have primary or specialty care... when it is time to call a specialist, primary, urgent care, or emergency room, what an Interdisciplinary Care Team (ICT) is, and what the community resources are'. This directly addresses providing education to parents and family members about the system of care and services, including social services (community resources).

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The MCP must maintain documentation of multidisciplinary comprehensive team assessments/reassessments and medical emergency plans.
explanation: The candidate addresses multidisciplinary team assessments and reassessments by stating the IDT is responsible for consolidating discipline-specific assessments into a Plan of Care after scheduled and unscheduled assessments. However, it does not explicitly mention the maintenance of 'medical emergency plans' or the general requirement to 'maintain documentation'.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The MCP must plan for the transition of youth to adult services by the age of 14, including sources of medical, vocational, financial, and support services and safety planning for youth with disabilities.
explanation: The policy explicitly states the MCP will 'Identify CCS-eligible Members who will require long-term health care transition planning' at 'Age fourteen (14)' for those 'reaching twenty-one (21) years of age', directly addressing the age and transition planning. However, it does not explicitly list 'vocational, financial, and support services' or 'safety planning for youth with disabilities' as required components of this planning, only medical services.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs are expected to work with local county CCS offices to ensure that Members receiving ECM services do not receive duplicative CCS services.
explanation: The policy states CalOptima Health shall ensure non-duplication of services provided through ECM and any other covered benefit, program, and/or delivery system, which broadly covers CCS services. However, it does not explicitly state that this non-duplication is achieved by working with local county CCS offices, which is a specific requirement of the obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs are required to demonstrate how they will prevent duplication in their respective MOC.
explanation: No candidate explicitly states how the MCP will prevent duplication in its Model of Care (MOC). While some candidates mention 'duplication,' they refer to different contexts such as clinical trials, MAC members, or provider information, not the MOC itself. The candidate that mentions 'MOC' does not address preventing duplication within it.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: Beginning July 1, 2024, MCPs should ensure that Members who meet ECM POF criteria are enrolled in ECM.
explanation: The policy states that 'ECM Providers shall provide ECM to Medi-Cal-only Members who meet eligibility criteria', which addresses the requirement for eligible members to receive ECM. However, it does not explicitly mention the effective date of 'Beginning July 1, 2024', making it incomplete coverage of the obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: Beginning July 1, 2024, MCPs must ensure that Members who meet ECM POF criteria are no longer enrolled in ECM and County-based TCM programs at the same time, except for a one-year exception from July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025 for cases where the Member is receiving County-based TCM (1) for addressing a communicable disease or (2) for the sole purpose of receiving a home visiting program supporting the healthy development and well-being of children and families.
explanation: The candidate states that the one-year exception for co-enrollment in ECM and County-based TCM programs runs from July 1, 2024, to June 20, 2025, which contradicts the obligation's specified end date of June 30, 2025.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs are responsible for analyzing whether Targeted Case Management (TCM) is duplicative of Enhanced Care Management (ECM) at both the county program level and the Member level.
explanation: The policy explicitly states that 'Data feed from DHCS when available is evaluated routinely to identify Members open in TCM and Case Management,' which directly describes the analysis of duplication between TCM and case management (including ECM) at both the program (routine evaluation of data feed) and member (identifying specific members) levels.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: If an MCP determines that the Targeted Case Management (TCM) is comprehensive and therefore substantially duplicative of Enhanced Care Management (ECM), the MCP must ensure that individuals do not receive both in that county.
explanation: The P&P states a general requirement to "ensure non-duplication of services provided through ECM and any other covered benefit." While Targeted Case Management (TCM) would fall under "any other covered benefit," the P&P does not explicitly mention TCM or the specific condition that the non-duplication applies "if an MCP determines that TCM is comprehensive and therefore substantially duplicative of ECM," as required by the obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs are expected to work with Local Governmental Agencies (LGAs) to ensure that Members receiving Enhanced Care Management (ECM) services do not receive duplicative Targeted Case Management (TCM) services.
explanation: The candidate states the plan will ensure non-duplication of ECM services with 'any other covered benefit, program, and/or delivery system,' which would include TCM. However, it does not explicitly name Targeted Case Management (TCM) or mention working with Local Governmental Agencies (LGAs) as required by the obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: For MCP Members who are identified as eligible for both County-based Targeted Case Management (TCM) and Enhanced Care Management (ECM), ECM should be the first option for comprehensive care management.
explanation: The candidate explicitly states, 'Beginning July 1, 2024, Members who meet ECM POF criteria should be enrolled in ECM and may no longer be enrolled in both TCM and ECM at the same time,' which directly supports the obligation that ECM should be the first option for comprehensive care management when a member is eligible for both.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: All Members who meet Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Population of Focus criteria should be referred to the Member’s MCP for ECM authorization.
explanation: The candidate states that a specific subset of members (those with Original Medicare, Medicare Advantage, or D-SNPs) "shall be authorized for ECM if they are referred" and meet POF criteria. While it addresses the referral and authorization for POF members, it does not explicitly cover "All Members" as required by the obligation, limiting its scope.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs are encouraged to contract with Local Governmental Agencies (LGAs) as Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Providers.
explanation: None of the provided P&P excerpts explicitly state that the MCP is encouraged to contract with Local Governmental Agencies (LGAs) as Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Providers. The candidates discuss various aspects of ECM services and provider responsibilities, but not the specific type of entity to contract with or an encouragement to do so.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The County-based TCM Program and ECM Provider must coordinate to ensure the non-duplication of services and associated billing when both are serving a Member at the same time.
explanation: The candidate states that 'case managers shall share information... and ensure non-duplication of services' for Members enrolled in both TCM and other case management, which includes ECM. This directly addresses the coordination and non-duplication of services. However, the obligation explicitly requires ensuring non-duplication of 'services AND associated billing,' and the candidate does not explicitly mention 'associated billing,' making it incomplete coverage.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The ECM Provider remains primarily responsible for the overall coordination across the physical and behavioral health delivery systems and social supports.
explanation: The P&P states, "The ECM Provider will work to ensure care is continuous and integrated among all service providers and refer to and follow up with primary care, physical and developmental health, mental health, SUD treatment, LTSS, oral health, Palliative Care, and necessary community-based and social services, including housing, as needed." This explicitly assigns the ECM Provider primary responsibility for overall coordination across physical health, behavioral health, and social supports.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: As of July 1, 2025, Members in the two exception cases who meet ECM POF criteria should be enrolled in ECM.
explanation: The candidate explicitly states that 'Beginning July 1, 2024, Members who meet ECM POF criteria should be enrolled in ECM and may no longer be enrolled in both TCM and ECM at the same time except for a one-year exception from July 1, 2024 to June 20, 2025 for cases where the Member is receiving County-Based TCM as follows: a) For addressing a communicable disease; or b) For the sole purpose of receiving a home visiting program'. This directly addresses the two exception cases and implies that as of July 1, 2025 (when the exception ends), these members should be enrolled in ECM, aligning with the obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The MCP will remain responsible for ensuring non-duplication of services when a Member chooses to remain enrolled in both County-based TCM and ECM programs until their care plan goals are achieved.
explanation: The obligation requires the MCP to ensure non-duplication of services when a Member chooses to remain enrolled in both County-based TCM and ECM programs until their care plan goals are achieved. However, candidate GG.1354-III.A.4 states that 'Beginning July 1, 2024, Members... may no longer be enrolled in both TCM and ECM at the same time except for a one-year exception,' which contradicts the premise of ongoing dual enrollment until care plan goals are met.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: Medi-Cal Managed Care Plans (MCPs) are strongly encouraged to contract with current County-based Targeted Case Management (TCM) providers who are becoming Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Providers.
explanation: No candidate explicitly states that the plan is strongly encouraged to contract with current County-based Targeted Case Management (TCM) providers who are becoming Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Providers. While some candidates discuss contracting with existing ECM providers for continuity of care, this does not address the specific encouragement to contract with transitioning TCM providers.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: Medi-Cal Managed Care Plans (MCPs) must continue to coordinate with County-based Targeted Case Management (TCM) programs to ensure non-duplication of enrollment, except for time-limited exceptions of County-based TCM for addressing communicable diseases and the sole purpose of home visiting programs supporting the healthy development and well-being of children and families.
explanation: The P&P excerpt explicitly states that members enrolled in County-based TCM may also be enrolled in ECM if services are not duplicated, directly addressing the non-duplication requirement. It then details a 'one-year exception' for dual enrollment in County-based TCM for 'addressing a communicable disease' or 'for the sole purpose of receiving a home visiting program supporting the health development and well-being of children and families,' which precisely matches the time-limited exceptions in the obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: Medi-Cal Managed Care Plans (MCPs) are required to work with counties to identify Members receiving Specialty Mental Health Services (SMHS) Targeted Case Management (TCM) and ensure non-duplication of services.
explanation: The policy explicitly states CalOptima Health shall ensure no duplication of services for Members enrolled in TCM through the HCA (county), and details that a DHCS data feed is evaluated to identify Members in TCM. It also requires case managers from both entities to share information to ensure non-duplication, directly addressing all aspects of the obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The Medi-Cal managed care plan (MCP) is required to work with the county to ensure non-duplication of services between ECM and SMHS ICC.
explanation: The candidate explicitly states that members enrolled in ECM and SMHS Intensive Care Coordination (ICC) for children may be enrolled in both "if services are not duplicated," directly addressing the non-duplication requirement between these two services. However, it does not explicitly state that the MCP is required to "work with the county" to ensure this non-duplication.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The ICC coordinator is responsible for working within the Child and Family Team (CFT) to ensure that plans from any of the system partners (MHPs, child welfare, juvenile, probation, education, etc.) are integrated to comprehensively address the identified goals and objectives.
explanation: The P&P states that the ICT facilitates communication and assists in developing the Member's care plan among various providers (medical, behavioral, social services, pharmacy, and ancillary). This implies an interdisciplinary approach and coordination of services from different areas, but it does not explicitly state that the coordinator is responsible for integrating *existing plans* from external system partners like child welfare or education.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The ICC Coordinator and the Child and Family Team (CFT) should reassess the strengths and needs of children and youth and their families, at least every 90 days, and as needed.
explanation: No candidate explicitly mentions the ICC Coordinator or Child and Family Team (CFT) reassessing the strengths and needs of children and youth and their families. While some candidates discuss reassessment or plan updates, they either specify different teams, different populations, or contradicting timeframes (e.g., every six months or annually) or lack the explicit 'at least every 90 days' requirement for the specified context.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The Managed Care Plan (MCP) must ensure that services provided under Enhanced Care Management (ECM) do not duplicate services provided under the Drug Medi-Cal Organized Delivery System (DMC-ODS) or Drug Medi-Cal (DMC) Program.
explanation: The policy explicitly states that members enrolled in Drug Medi-Cal Organized Delivery System (DMC-ODS) and Drug Medi-Cal (DMC) programs may also be enrolled in ECM, 'if services are not duplicated', directly addressing the obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: Managed Care Plans (MCPs) may not exclude Members from Enhanced Care Management (ECM) solely because they are participants in a Full Service Partnership (FSP) program.
explanation: The P&P explicitly states that "CalOptima Health Members enrolled in the following programs may also be enrolled in ECM, if services are not duplicated: ... i. Full Service Partnership (FSP) Funded by Mental Health Services Act (MHSA);", directly addressing that FSP participation does not exclude members from ECM.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: Managed Care Plans (MCPs) and counties overseeing Mental Health Services Act (MHSA) funded Full Service Partnership (FSP) programs must collaborate to share data, identify Medi-Cal managed care adult, child, and youth Members served by both ECM and FSP programs, and ensure that services and funding are not duplicated between ECM and FSP programs.
explanation: The policy states CalOptima Health shall ensure non-duplication of services through ECM and "any other covered benefit, program, and/or delivery system," which would include FSP programs. However, it does not explicitly mention FSP, collaboration with counties, data sharing, or the identification of members served by both ECM and FSP programs, thus providing incomplete coverage of the obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: Managed Care Plans (MCPs) must ensure that services are not duplicated between Enhanced Care Management (ECM) and the Health Care Program for Children in Foster Care (HCPCFC).
explanation: The P&P explicitly states that members enrolled in the Health Care Program for Children in Foster Care (HCPCFC) may also be enrolled in ECM 'if services are not duplicated', directly addressing the obligation for non-duplication between these two programs.

obligation: MCPs will need to add a disclaimer in the Directory stating that both ECM and Community Supports require prior authorization and are limited to Members who meet specific eligibility criteria.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: ECM Providers should have formal agreements and processes in place to engage and cooperate with area hospitals, primary care practices, behavioral health Providers, Specialists, and other entities, including Community Supports Providers, to coordinate care as appropriate to each Member.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: ECM Providers must have the capacity to provide culturally appropriate and timely in-person care management activities.
explanation: The candidate explicitly states that CalOptima Health shall ensure ECM Providers 'Have capacity to provide culturally appropriate and timely in-person care management activities,' directly matching the obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: ECM Providers and Lead Care Managers must meet Members in a physical location that is most convenient and desirable for the Member to engage in services and from a medical management and plan of care perspective.
explanation: The P&P explicitly states, "ECM Providers and Lead Care Managers shall meet ECM Members where they are in terms of the physical location that is most convenient and desirable for the Member to engage in services and from a medical management and plan of care perspective," which directly matches the obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: ECM Providers must be able to communicate with Members in a culturally and linguistically appropriate and accessible way.
explanation: The P&P explicitly states, "ECM Providers shall communicate with Members in culturally and linguistically appropriate and accessible ways," directly matching the obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: ECM Providers must be able to respectfully engage with Members who have been historically marginalized and/or are experiencing health disparities.
explanation: The P&P explicitly states that ECM Providers must serve Members with "respect for Member choice and cultural diversity" and provide services with "cultural and linguistic competency and humility," directly addressing respectful engagement with historically marginalized populations.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCP Network Providers (including those that will operate as ECM or Community Supports Providers) are required to enroll as a Medi-Cal Provider only if there is a state-level enrollment pathway for them to do so.
explanation: The candidate explicitly states that 'All Network Providers, including those who will operate as Supervising Providers of CHW Services, are required to enroll as Medi-Cal Providers... if there is a state-level enrollment pathway for them to do so,' directly matching the obligation's requirement and condition for Network Providers, including Community Supports Providers.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: Providers with a state-level Medi-Cal enrollment pathway must enroll through the DHCS Provider Enrollment Division.
explanation: The obligation states that providers 'must enroll through the DHCS Provider Enrollment Division'. However, the P&P excerpt states that state-level enrollment pathways are available 'either through the Department of Health Care Services’ (DHCS) Provider Enrollment Division (PED) or another state department with a recognized enrollment pathway', which offers an alternative and thus contradicts the exclusive requirement.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The MCP can choose to have a separate enrollment process for Providers with a state-level Medi-Cal enrollment pathway.
explanation: The candidate explicitly states that 'CalOptima Health shall have the option to develop and implement a managed care provider screening and enrollment process... or CalOptima Health may direct Network Providers to enroll through a state-level enrollment pathway.' This directly aligns with the obligation that the MCP can choose to have a separate enrollment process for providers with a state-level Medi-Cal enrollment pathway.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: ECM Providers who serve the Justice-Involved POF are required to become a Medi-Cal enrolled provider.
explanation: The P&P states that CalOptima Health shall ensure continuity of care for individuals transitioning from incarceration 'in accordance with the California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) Policy and Operational Guide for Planning and Implementing the CalAIM Justice-Involved Initiative'. This implies adherence to the DHCS guide, which likely contains the provider enrollment requirement, but the P&P itself does not explicitly state that ECM Providers serving this POF must be Medi-Cal enrolled.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The MCP must vet ECM Providers that do not have a state-level enrollment pathway in order to participate as ECM Providers.
explanation: The policy explicitly states, 'If no Medi-Cal/Medicaid enrollment pathway exists, CalOptima Health shall verify the qualifications of the provider or provider organization to ensure they meet the standards and capabilities to be an ECM Provider,' directly addressing the obligation to vet ECM Providers without a state-level enrollment pathway.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The MCP must vet ECM and Community Supports Providers without a state-level pathway to Medi-Cal enrollment in order for them to participate as “in-network” ECM and/or Community Supports Providers.
explanation: Chunk GG.1356-III.G.2 explicitly states the requirement to vet ECM Providers when no state-level enrollment pathway exists. However, it does not explicitly address Community Supports Providers, leading to incomplete coverage for the overall obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs should use and build on the processes they have already established for vetting the qualifications and experience of ECM Providers.
explanation: The P&P explicitly states that CalOptima Health shall credential ECM Providers in accordance with existing policies (GG.1650 and GG.1651) and consider additional factors as part of its process for vetting their qualifications and experience. This directly aligns with the obligation to use and build on established processes for vetting ECM Provider qualifications and experience.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: To include an ECM and Community Supports Provider in their networks when there is no state-level Medi-Cal enrollment pathway, MCPs are required to vet the qualifications of the Provider or Provider organization to ensure they can meet the standards and capabilities required to be an ECM or Community Supports Provider.
explanation: The P&P explicitly states that if no Medi-Cal enrollment pathway exists, CalOptima Health shall verify the qualifications of the Provider or Provider organization to ensure they meet the standards and capabilities to be a Community Supports Provider. A parallel policy (GG.1356-III.G.2) provides the same requirement for ECM Providers.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs must submit Policies and Procedures for how they will vet the qualifications of ECM and Community Supports Providers in their submission of Part 2 of the MOC.
explanation: The candidate explicitly details a process for 'vetting the qualifications and experience of Community Supports Providers,' including specific factors to consider. However, it does not explicitly outline a similar vetting process for ECM Providers, which are also part of the obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs must create and implement their own processes for vetting ECM and Community Supports Providers.
explanation: The P&P explicitly describes CalOptima Health's process for vetting Community Supports Providers, including factors considered. However, it does not explicitly detail a similar vetting process for ECM Providers, only listing qualifications or oversight activities for them in other sections.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide

explanation: The policy states ECM is provided "primarily through in-person interaction in settings that are most appropriate for the Member," which directly addresses the in-person requirement and indirectly suggests community settings, but does not explicitly state "in the community" for the provision of ECM services.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: Any request for a time-bound exception to use MCP staff to deliver ECM services must be submitted in accordance with DHCS guidelines.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: Any request for a time-bound exception to use MCP staff to deliver ECM services must evidence one or more of the following reasons: insufficient ECM Providers or lack of experienced ECM Providers for specific Populations of Focus, a justified quality-of-care concern with qualified ECM Providers, inability of the Contractor and ECM Provider(s) to agree on contracted rates, unwilling or unresponsive potential ECM Provider(s), or inability of Provider(s) to comply with Medi-Cal enrollment or Contractor’s vetting processes.
explanation: No candidate explicitly states that the listed reasons justify a time-bound exception to use MCP staff to deliver ECM services. While some candidates discuss provider capacity or contracting issues, they do not link these to the specific exception of using MCP staff.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: During any exception period approved by DHCS, the MCP must take steps to continually develop and increase the capacity of its ECM Provider Network.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: After the initial one-year exception period, the MCP must submit a new exception request to DHCS for DHCS review and approval on a case-by-case basis.
explanation: No candidate explicitly addresses the requirement to submit a new exception request to DHCS for review and approval after an initial one-year exception period. docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: ECM Providers must use a care management documentation system or process that supports the documentation and integration of physical, behavioral, social service and administrative data and information from other entities to support the management and maintenance of a Member care plan that can be shared with other Providers and organizations involved in each Member’s care.
explanation: The candidate explicitly states that ECM Providers must 'Use a care management documentation system that supports the documentation and integration of physical, behavioral, social service, and administrative data and information from other entities to support the management and maintenance of ECM Member care plans' and 'Maintain processes for sharing ECM Member care plans with other Providers and organizations involved in each ECM Member’s care, as appropriate,' directly addressing all aspects of the obligation.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs may not require ECM Providers to utilize an MCP portal for documentation of ECM services.
explanation: The candidate states that the ECM Provider shall 'document it in their system of record', which implies they are not required to use an MCP portal for this specific documentation. docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs must be able to accept data on documentation of ECM services when it is submitted in a standardized, machine-readable format.
explanation: The policy explicitly states that ECM Providers are expected to submit ECM Encounters to CalOptima Health using 'national standard specifications and code sets to be defined by DHCS,' which directly addresses the requirement for accepting data on documentation of ECM services in a standardized, machine-readable format.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs should not otherwise require Providers to use the portal for purposes other than exchanging Member information lists and authorization information.
explanation: No candidate explicitly addresses the obligation that MCPs should not require providers to use a portal for purposes other than exchanging member information lists and authorization information. docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs must pay contracted ECM Providers for the provision of ECM in accordance with contracts established between MCPs and each ECM Provider.
explanation: The candidate explicitly states that 'CalOptima Health shall make an ECM supplemental payment to an ECM Provider at rates set forth in the Contract for Health Care Services, in accordance with the terms and conditions of this policy,' directly addressing the obligation for MCPs to pay contracted ECM Providers in accordance with established contracts.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs must ensure that ECM Providers are eligible to receive payment when ECM is initiated for any given.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs must pay 90% of all clean claims within 30 days of the date of receipt and 99% of all clean claims within 90 days.
explanation: The candidate states the plan shall 'process and adjudicate' 90% of Clean Claims within 30 days and 99% of claims (not explicitly 'clean claims') within 90 days. This is relevant but does not explicitly state 'pay' as required by the obligation, and the scope for the 99% target is broader than 'clean claims'.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs must reimburse claims or any portion of any claim as soon as practicable, but no later than 30 working days after receipt of the claim.
explanation: The obligation requires claims to be reimbursed no later than 30 working days. However, the P&P states that 100% of contracted and non-contracted claims shall be processed and adjudicated within 45 business days, which is a longer timeframe than required.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs must pay all claims within contractually mandated statutory timeframes.
explanation: The excerpt states that a Health Network shall 'adjudicate claims... in accordance with the Health Network’s contract... as well as... applicable laws and regulations,' which directly covers the obligation to pay all claims within contractually mandated statutory timeframes.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs must maintain sufficient claims processing, tracking, and payment system capabilities.
explanation: The candidate explicitly states that 'CalOptima Health shall maintain sufficient claims processing, tracking and payment systems capability,' directly matching the obligation's requirement for maintaining sufficient claims processing, tracking, and payment system capabilities.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs are required to train their contracted network of ECM Providers on how to submit a clean claim.
explanation: The P&P states that CalOptima Health shall provide 'training and technical assistance to participating ECM Provider care management staff' (GG.1356-II.H.1), which includes 'operational and focused trainings' (GG.1356-III.F.1). While this suggests training is provided, it does not explicitly state that the training covers 'how to submit a clean claim,' requiring an inference that 'operational trainings' or 'technical assistance' would include this specific topic.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs are responsible for driving ECM enrollment through community-based referrals.
explanation: The P&P states that CalOptima Health (MCP) "shall inform CalOptima Health network Providers and community-based organizations about the referral process and the CalOptima Health ECM Referral form." This directly demonstrates the MCP's responsibility for driving ECM enrollment through community-based referrals by actively disseminating information about the referral process to these entities.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs are responsible for regularly and proactively identifying Members who may benefit from ECM.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs must consider Members’ health care utilization; needs across physical, behavioral, developmental and oral health; health risks and needs due to social determinants of health (SDOH); and Long-Term Services and Supports (LTSS) needs.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs may not require nor request community partners or ECM Providers to submit supplemental eligibility checklists, outreach authorization forms, ICD-10 codes, additional proof of homelessness, Treatment Authorization Request (TAR) forms, or other supplemental information beyond the information provided in the ECM Referral.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide

explanation: The policy states CalOptima Health informs Members, their family, guardian, caregiver, and authorized support persons about the referral process, including how to submit a request for ECM. This partially addresses the obligation by covering a subset of the required audience and the process to request ECM, but it does not explicitly state that CalOptima Health informs all specified parties (e.g., ECM Providers, Community Supports Providers, other Providers, CBOs) about ECM or the ECM Populations of Focus.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: MCPs must consider requests for ECM on behalf of Members from Members, their families, guardians, caregivers, ECM Providers, Community Supports Providers, other Providers, and CBOs.
explanation: The P&P explicitly states that CalOptima Health "shall allow a Member and/or a family member, guardian, Authorized Representative, caregiver, a Member’s authorized support person, ECM Providers, Community Supports Providers, other Providers, and community-based organizations (CBOs) and/or external entity to request ECM on the Member’s behalf and shall accept referrals." docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: Managed Care Plans (MCPs) must rely on a combination of information provided by DHCS on a regular basis and data internal to the plan.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The MCP must ensure that authorization or a decision not to authorize ECM occurs as soon as possible, specifically within five working days for routine authorizations and within 72 hours for expedited requests.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The MCP must automatically authorize ECM for a newly enrolled Member if any of the following conditions apply: 1. The previous MCP informs the new MCP that the Member received ECM during the last 90 days of enrollment in the previous MCP and did not subsequently either meet graduation criteria or choose to discontinue ECM; 2. Historical utilization data provided to the new MCP by DHCS (referred to as the Plan Data Feed) reveals one or more ECM Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) codes for ECM services delivered during the last 90 days of enrollment in the previous MCP; 3. The Member, family, or Authorized Representative notifies the new MCP that the Member received ECM during the last 90 days of enrollment in the previous MCP and wishes to continue to do so; 4. The Member’s previous ECM Provider notifies the new MCP that the Member received ECM during the last 90 days of enrollment in the previous MCP and recommends continuation of ECM; or 5. The new MCP becomes aware that a newly enrolled Member received ECM during the last 90 days of enrollment in the previous MCP, in any other way.
explanation: The candidate explicitly states that the MCP shall "Authorize the Member for ECM upon" the exact five conditions listed in the obligation, including notification from the previous MCP, DHCS data, member/family/representative notification, previous ECM provider notification, or awareness through any other way, all within the last 90 days of previous enrollment.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The new MCP must not implement any other steps to authorize ECM for newly enrolled Members who were receiving ECM in their previous MCP (including obtaining consent to ECM services) if any of the listed conditions for automatic authorization apply.
explanation: The policy lists the specific conditions upon which a member shall be authorized for ECM, which aligns with the 'listed conditions for automatic authorization'. docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The new MCP must assign the Member to an ECM Provider for outreach and continuation of ECM, in accordance with its DHCS-approved ECM Policies and Procedures.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The new MCP is encouraged to contract with the member’s ECM Provider when its network does not align with the member’s previous MCP.

It further clarifies that 'CalOptima Health shall inform DHCS when Continuity of Care contracting efforts do not result in agreement with ECM provider,' directly addressing the encouragement to contract with the member's previous ECM provider when the network does not align.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: The new MCP should apply its usual Policies and Procedures for reassessment against discontinuation criteria to determine if and when the Member may be stepped down from ECM.
explanation: The P&P excerpt explicitly states that the 'ECM Provider should reassess Members against their ECM discontinuation criteria... to evaluate whether Members are ready to transition out of ECM,' directly addressing the obligation to apply policies for reassessment against discontinuation criteria to determine stepping down from ECM.

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide

docTitle: CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Policy Guide
obligation: If a Member’s existing care management program chooses not to serve as the ECM Provider, the MCP must ensure the Member receives ECM services and does not receive duplicative care management services or be subject to processes that duplicate what the existing model is already doing (e.g., screening and assessment).

obligation: The MCP must notify the Member’s PCP, if different from the ECM Provider, of the assignment to the ECM Provider, within ten (10) business days of the date of assignment.

obligation: MCPs must not require ECM Providers or their own staff to obtain Member (and/or parent, guardian, caretaker) consent to participate (in writing or otherwise) as a condition of initiating delivery of ECM, unless required by federal law.

obligation: MCPs should reassess Members against their ECM discontinuation criteria, not the ECM Population of Focus eligibility criteria, to evaluate whether Members are ready to transition out of ECM.
